History and Physical (H&P – Detailed)

Consult Summary:
19-year-old female with 3-day history of dysuria, mild lower abdominal cramping, and brief hematuria; clinically consistent with an uncomplicated urinary tract infection (UTI).

History:
• Presenting complaint: Burning/stinging pain on micturition for “a few days” (~3 days).  
• Associated symptoms:  
  – Mild cramp-like suprapubic discomfort when voiding.  
  – Small amount of blood in urine earlier today.  
  – Malodorous urine.  
• Denies: Flank/back pain, urinary frequency or urgency, fever/chills, nausea, vomiting, bowel changes or diarrhoea.  
• Sexual history: Sexually active with one partner (boyfriend, 2 months); condom use; never had an STI screen; last menstrual period “a couple of weeks ago” (doctor restated 3 weeks – conflict noted); does not believe she is pregnant.  
• No known precipitating factors; symptoms not relieved by OTC bicarbonate product.

Past Medical History:
• Irritable bowel syndrome (IBS) – no recent flare reported.

Medications:
• None regular.  
• OTC bicarbonate preparation taken recently – “didn’t help” (dose/route/frequency not documented).

Allergies:
• Clindamycin – causes swelling (probable angio-edema).

Social History:
• College student (biology major); lives in a flat with friends near college.  
• Non-smoker.  
• Social alcohol use on weekends; denies other substance use.

Family History:
• No known renal, bladder, or gastrointestinal disorders reported.

Physical Examination:
• No physical exam or vitals documented (tele-consult).

Investigations:
• None performed/available during this visit.

Assessment & Plan:
Issue 1: Suspected uncomplicated lower urinary tract infection (cystitis).  
  – Empiric oral antibiotics: Nitrofurantoin OR Trimethoprim, 1 tablet twice daily for 3 days (exact drug and dose not documented).  
  – Encourage increased oral fluids; consider cranberry juice.  
  – Counselled on avoidance of sexual intercourse until symptoms resolve; continue condom use thereafter.  
  – Safety-net advice: return/call if fever, flank/back pain, worsening symptoms, or no improvement by end of week (possible pyelonephritis or resistant organism).  
  – If symptoms persist, arrange review, repeat urine testing, possible culture and sensitivity.  

Issue 2: Pregnancy exclusion.  
  – Advised to perform a pregnancy test if any doubt or if symptoms persist/worsen.  

Issue 3: Sexual health.  
  – Offered information about first-time STI screening; to arrange at future convenient time.

General Plan items:  
  – Document Clindamycin allergy in medical record.  
  – Reinforce good hydration and urinary hygiene measures.

Quality checks:
• Missing but expected: Vital signs, abdominal/loin examination, urinalysis or culture, medication reconciliation of all OTC products.  
• Internal conflicts: LMP reported as “a couple of weeks ago” vs clinician restating “three weeks ago.”  
• Transcript quality: Clear; minor overlaps/inaudible sections but clinical content intact.
